source.interpretation: Pinned source records canonical route, SIWE, refresh, JWKS, wallet-identity, and granular-permission evidence. Source behavior is not automatically a safe production target; A1 and A2 fail-closed constraints take precedence where source evidence is incomplete.

targetSnapshot.interpretation: Immutable pre-remediation target authority consumed by A2.3i. The ref records provenance only; the exact commit, blobs, and anchors prove the historical A2.3h findings and do not describe current runtime status.

evidence.finding: All eleven recorded shapes exist, but the router has no strict direct-service authorization classifier.

Candidate access and refresh credentials use the same noncanonical claim shape and verifier and do not expose the canonical RS256 issuer, kid, exact audience, scope, wallet-address, or credential-type contract.
The shared extracted-service verifier defines the canonical fail-closed access-token boundary, but services/identity does not consume it.

anchors: refresh cookie is never accepted as an access token
evidence.finding: A1 proves hermetic contracts only and explicitly leaves live SIWE, nonce, durable rotation/revocation, and production behavior blocked.
The machine-readable A1 gate prohibits promoting hermetic evidence to production readiness.
The A2 inventory records the exact eleven identity route decisions and existing canonical admin permission names.

routes.intendedBoundary: anonymous exact GET/HEAD health only; strip credentials and spoofable identity headers before dispatch
routes.observed: The handler is anonymous, but the service has no strict method/path/arity normalization boundary.

routes.intendedBoundary: anonymous public SIWE bootstrap only after bounded input, throttling, exact relying-party fields, and durable single-use nonce issuance are proven
routes.ownership: requested wallet is a challenge selector only and proves no identity
routes.observed: The candidate writes a Redis nonce with TTL, but public request bounds, route throttling, durable parity, and the complete SIWE binding contract are unproven.

routes.intendedBoundary: anonymous public verification bootstrap that atomically consumes the exact stored challenge only after signature and full SIWE binding validation
routes.audience: one server-approved BFF audience selected by a proven flow
routes.ownership: signed SIWE address equals stored challenge wallet and the issued token subject/wallet
routes.observed: The candidate performs Redis GET then DEL and deletes before signature verification; issued tokens do not satisfy the canonical A1/A2 contract.

routes.intendedBoundary: refresh credential only; atomically consume and rotate a durable server-side session while retaining its server-bound frontend or admin audience
routes.audience: server-bound original BFF audience; never caller-selected and never both
routes.ownership: durable refresh session subject equals the canonical wallet subject reloaded server-side
routes.observed: The candidate verifies a long-lived JWT with the same verifier and claim shape as access tokens and has no durable consume/rotate/revoke store.

routes.intendedBoundary: canonical RS256/JWKS access token with exactly one frontend or admin audience
routes.ownership: response wallet/subject is derived exclusively from the verified access token and resolved server-side
routes.observed: The candidate accepts its noncanonical shared-secret token and queries a candidate UUID subject; it does not consume the shared access-token verifier.

routes.intendedBoundary: unreachable in production and production-like builds; return 404 before body parsing, SQL, or token issuance
routes.observed: A mutable environment flag can enable caller-selected demo identity creation and real candidate token issuance.

routes.intendedBoundary: canonical RS256/JWKS access token with exact admin audience and granular read permission
routes.ownership: admin operator identity comes only from the verified token; listed user identity is server-derived
routes.observed: The candidate uses a database role named admin instead of exact audience plus canonical permission.

routes.intendedBoundary: canonical RS256/JWKS access token with exact admin audience and granular create permission
routes.ownership: operator is verified; target wallet and allowed attributes are validated server-side and never grant caller-invented authority
routes.observed: The candidate authorizes by admin role and accepts caller-selected roles without the pinned granular permission and audited provisioning contract.

routes.intendedBoundary: canonical RS256/JWKS access token with exact admin audience and granular read permission
routes.ownership: path id is a selector only; canonical wallet/user mapping is resolved and authorized server-side
routes.observed: The candidate detail handler has no authorization check and its UUID identity does not establish parity with the pinned wallet-address authority.

routes.intendedBoundary: canonical RS256/JWKS access token with exact admin audience and granular update permission
routes.ownership: operator and target identity are server-derived; role/permission changes follow backend authority and audit rules
routes.observed: The candidate authorizes by admin role and can replace caller-selected roles without the granular permission or canonical permission model.

routes.intendedBoundary: canonical RS256/JWKS access token with exact admin audience and granular delete permission
routes.ownership: operator and target identity are server-derived; deletion semantics must preserve canonical authority, sessions, dependencies, and audit
routes.observed: The candidate authorizes by admin role and performs a direct delete without proven session revocation, dependency, audit, or canonical identity semantics.

invariants.rule: Only exact normalized method/path/arity shapes reach a handler; encoded ambiguity, reserved dynamic segments, extra slashes, and unknown shapes fail before authentication or I/O.
Access credentials use canonical RS256, kid/JWKS lookup, issuer, expiry/nbf/iat, exactly one approved BFF audience, sub equal to canonical wallet, and canonical scope grammar.

Refresh credentials are distinguishable from access credentials, stored durably, bound to subject and one BFF audience, atomically consumed and rotated, and revocable on logout or account security changes.
SIWE verification binds the exact stored message, nonce, canonical wallet, relying-party domain, URI, chain, issued/expiry times, and signature before one atomic nonce-consumption transition.
Public bootstrap bodies, time, concurrency, and request rates are bounded and yield typed non-secret error responses.
Admin routes require the exact admin audience and the existing granular permission recorded for each operation; a database role or spoofable header is never authority.
The canonical identity key remains the normalized wallet address unless a reviewed, migrated, reversible server-side wallet-to-ID mapping proves equivalent semantics.
Demo identity and token issuance are structurally unreachable in production and production-like configurations.
All identity schema changes are reviewed additive migrations; startup never creates or rewrites authority tables and environment variables never mutate admin authority.
Live database, Redis, JWKS rotation, BFF cookie, logout, revocation, cross-owner, cross-audience, shadow, cutover, and rollback behavior is proven before traffic migration.

blockers.summary: No strict direct-service method/path/arity classifier or spoofable-header stripping boundary exists.
blockers.resolution: Install a tested fail-closed classifier before handlers and all database, Redis, token, or signature work.

blockers.summary: The candidate identity service uses a defaultable shared-secret JWT configuration.
blockers.resolution: Use the canonical RS256 issuer/key lifecycle and refuse missing or unsafe production key configuration.

blockers.summary: Candidate claims omit the canonical issuer, kid, exact audience, scope, wallet-address, and required validity contract.
blockers.resolution: Issue the A1 canonical claims and verify them through the same accepted RS256/JWKS contract.

blockers.summary: Candidate access and refresh JWTs have the same claims and verifier, so credential type is not enforced.
blockers.resolution: Make refresh credentials unambiguously distinct and ensure access tokens can never enter refresh paths.

blockers.summary: No durable refresh session, atomic rotation, old-token rejection, reuse handling, or logout/account revocation exists in the candidate.
blockers.resolution: Implement and test the durable A1 lifecycle with atomic transactions and generic failure responses.

blockers.summary: Candidate Redis GET then DEL is not an atomic, durable single-use nonce transition.
blockers.resolution: Use an atomic compare-and-consume operation bound to the stored challenge and expiry.

blockers.summary: The candidate deletes a nonce before signature validation, enabling invalid attempts to consume a legitimate challenge.
blockers.resolution: Validate all signed fields and signature, then atomically transition the exact unused nonce while preventing concurrent reuse.

blockers.summary: Full parity for stored message, requested chain, signed chain, address, domain, URI, issued-at, expiry, and audience selection is not proven.
blockers.resolution: Lock and test every SIWE relying-party and wallet binding against the accepted source/A1 contract.

blockers.summary: Challenge and SIWE bodies, rates, concurrency, signature cost, and error behavior are not bounded at the candidate router.
blockers.resolution: Add explicit size/time/rate/concurrency limits with deterministic typed errors and abuse telemetry.

blockers.summary: A mutable environment flag can expose demo user creation and real candidate token issuance.
blockers.resolution: Remove the production route or compile it out; production-like configurations must return 404 before body and I/O.

blockers.summary: Candidate admin checks use a database role instead of exact admin audience plus operation-specific permission.
blockers.resolution: Use the shared verifier and the existing admin:users read/create/update/delete grants recorded by A2.

blockers.summary: GET /users/{id} reaches a user record without any authorization check.
blockers.resolution: Require exact admin audience and admin:users:read before parsing the selector or touching SQL.

blockers.summary: Candidate UUID subjects and {id} selectors are not reconciled with the pinned wallet-address identity authority.
blockers.resolution: Choose and migrate a canonical server-side wallet/user mapping with reconciliation, foreign/missing hiding, and rollback.

blockers.summary: Startup environment configuration can mutate an existing user into an admin role, and user mutations accept role arrays.
blockers.resolution: Move all authority changes behind backend permission logic, validation, durable audit, idempotency, and explicit operator workflows.

blockers.summary: The candidate creates its users authority table at runtime and has no reviewed migration/reconciliation proof.
blockers.resolution: Move schema ownership to additive migrations and prove data mapping, constraints, reconciliation, and rollback offline then in an approved disposable environment.

blockers.summary: Candidate issuance has no canonical kid/JWKS discovery, rotation, overlap, cache, unknown-kid, or rollback behavior.
blockers.resolution: Adopt the canonical issuer and prove current/backup key rotation and service verifier behavior without exposing private material.

blockers.summary: Gateway split, BFF audience selection, cookie pairing, refresh, logout, and token-free browser behavior are not proven end to end for the candidate service.
blockers.resolution: Complete A1/A2 integration fixtures, then disposable live and production-shaped rehearsal with explicit rollback.

blockers.summary: Source-compatible request/response/status, secret-handling, audit, validation, and conflict semantics are incomplete.
blockers.resolution: Lock typed DTOs/envelopes/statuses, redact credentials, and prove success plus denial/error/conflict cases before enabling routes.

blockers.summary: Create/update/delete behavior has no canonical account lifecycle, dependency, session-revocation, tombstone, or recovery contract.
blockers.resolution: Specify backend-owned lifecycle transitions, referential behavior, session effects, audit, idempotency, and recovery before mutations execute.

blockers.summary: No database, Redis, live JWKS, service, cross-audience, cross-owner, concurrency, shadow, canary, cutover, or rollback proof was run.
blockers.resolution: After static blockers close, run separately approved disposable integration and production-shaped evidence; do not infer readiness from this audit.

E02 add strict fail-closed route classification and public-body/rate bounds
E03 adopt canonical RS256 issuer and shared access-token verifier
E04 implement atomic durable SIWE nonce issue/verify/consume semantics
E05 implement durable audience-bound refresh rotation, reuse rejection, and revocation
E06 enforce exact admin audience and existing granular permissions before selectors or SQL
E07 migrate and reconcile wallet/user/session/nonce schemas additively with rollback
E08 lock typed request, response, status, audit, redaction, and account-lifecycle semantics
E09 run hermetic negative, concurrency, and rotation fixtures
E10 run approved disposable PostgreSQL/Redis/JWKS/BFF integration and source-shadow comparison
E11 rehearse canary, observability, revocation emergency path, and rollback
E12 request explicit production deployment approval only after every STOP is closed
